##: The installer is a PE with the payload stored as a ZIP resource; 7-Zip opens it directly, so the URL carries a #/dl.7z fragment to make Scoop unpack instead of execute it.

Unpacking yields install\{YYAnchor.exe, Launcher.xml, <version>\}; the vendor layout is kept on purpose because the 289 KiB YYAnchor.exe is a launcher that loads the versioned mainframe.dll named by Launcher.xml.

The payload carries the embedded OBS the app starts as obs\bin\64bit\yyobs.exe. Its browser module needs libcef.dll, which the vendor setup copies from the payload root into obs\bin\64bit after unpacking; extraction alone leaves obs-browser.dll unloadable, so post_install repeats that copy.
The manifest version follows the CDN directory (X.Y.Z.0), not the build number in the PE (3.19.0.5576), so the autoupdate URL substitution stays valid.

No checkver: the vendor gates every version source behind request signing. v.yy.com resolves the installer through lpfm2-download.yy.com/installer/getInstaller, which answers 204 'no installer' outside the mainland service, and up.yy.com/api/check/yyanchor/check4update needs an MD5 nonce and returns 'no rule found' for every sourceVersion tried. Bump version and hash by hand.

Virtual camera registration is deliberately opt-in: regsvr32 writes HKLM\Software\Classes and needs UAC, so doing it in post_install would break unattended 'scoop update *'. installer.script writes register-virtualcam.ps1 into the app dir instead, matching the extras/obs-studio and streaming-tool manifests in this bucket.

YYVCamService.exe --regYYVCam is not reused: it resolves \Stable\YYVirtualCam*.ax through HKCU\Software\Duowan\YYAnchor, a layout the Scoop package does not have. The generated script calls regsvr32 on the unpacked files directly; obs-virtualsource.dll is registered with /n /i:1 to install one OBS camera through DllInstall.
description: YY Anchor live-streaming studio with virtual camera output for Windows
notes: Only the x64 build is published.
The installer build is 3.19.0.5576, as shown in the app; the manifest version tracks the CDN directory 3.19.0.0 so the download and autoupdate URLs stay valid.
The unpacked layout is the vendor one: YYAnchor.exe (launcher), Launcher.xml and the versioned payload directory. Do not flatten it.
The bundled update.exe updates the app in place, which adds a new version directory under the Scoop app folder. Reinstalling with 'scoop install yy-anchor -f' returns to the packaged build.

The virtual camera is NOT registered by Scoop. The payload ships five self-registering DirectShow filters: YYVirtualCam.ax, YYVirtualCamMul.ax, their _x86 twins, and obs\bin\64bit\obs-virtualsource.dll (which provides 'OBS Virtual Cam' / 'OBS-Camera'). Only the vendor setup registers them.

Enable the camera by running '& "$dir\register-virtualcam.ps1"' from any PowerShell; the script self-elevates via UAC. Pass '-Unregister' before uninstalling, and re-run it after every yy-anchor update because the registered paths include the versioned build folder.
obs-virtualsource.dll is 64-bit only; the _x86 .ax filters are what 32-bit programs see. Registration needs administrator rights because it writes HKLM\Software\Classes.

Launching the app can hand off to the vendor setup, which installs a second, per-user copy under %LOCALAPPDATA%\duowan\yyanchor and repoints HKCU\Software\Duowan\YYAnchor at it. That copy sits outside Scoop and needs its own Uninstall.exe to be removed.
User data, logs and cache live in the YYAnchor folders under %APPDATA% and %LOCALAPPDATA%, so nothing is persisted by Scoop.

script: if (-not $vc) { throw 'Versioned payload folder with obs\bin\64bit not found.' }
Write-Host 'Done. Restart camera apps; re-run this script after each yy-anchor update.'
